judge.text:
- The close permit reads `context.input.site_id` as a plain string, but the list permit reads `context.input.site_id.typeChoice0`. Under either encoding, one permit can never match, so the agent is denied either closing at MAIN or listing MAIN, which the intent allows.
- The self-approval check `context.approval.approver != principal` compares the approver against the principal entity. If `approver` is a string, Cedar treats the comparison as always unequal, so the check passes even when the agent approved the work order itself. The intent forbids this.
